# Pressure builds on Iran as Trump boosts U.S. military presence

[Add Spokesman-Review on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=spokesman.com)

By Peter Martin, Patrick Sykes, Fiona MacDonald and Samy Adghirni Bloomberg

Seven months into war with the U.S., Iran’s leaders are feeling the strain.

Inflation in the Islamic Republic is almost 90%, oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are recovering despite continued Iranian attacks, and President Donald Trump is sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. A U.S. blockade is choking off Iran’s crude exports, while diplomacy remains deadlocked.

Even for a regime accustomed to sanctions and economic hardship, that is a punishing combination.

The squeeze matters because it could force Iran into a choice: make concessions to try to revive peace talks or escalate a conflict that’s already damaging its economy. Trump’s domestic situation will likely influence Tehran’s thinking. The U.S. leader also is in a bind, with oil around $100 a barrel and high fuel prices hurting U.S. consumers ahead of November midterm elections.

## Russia rejects limited Black Sea truce

# Russia rejects limited Black Sea truce

##### MOSCOW

![Russia rejects limited Black Sea truce](https://static.hurriyetdailynews.com/images/placeholder-img.jpg)

[Russia](/index/russia "Russia") has rejected a limited [Black Sea](/index/black-sea "Black Sea") ceasefire as Türkiye and the United Nations seek to arrange talks, with the Kremlin insisting on a broader settlement while saying it remains open to dialogue.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Oct. 2 that Moscow was aware of the Turkish-U.N. initiative but had no specific details. He accused Kiev of refusing comprehensive agreements.

“Piecemeal arrangements cannot bring us closer to a peaceful settlement,” Peskov said.

He said Russia would continue trying to stop military equipment, ammunition and fuel reaching Ukraine by sea. Moscow remained open to discussions with Türkiye, India and Egypt on Black Sea security, he added, though no concrete talks were under way.

His remarks followed President Vladimir Putin’s rejection of proposals linking a halt to Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries with an end to Russian strikes on shipping serving Ukraine. Speaking at the Valdai Discussion Club on Oct. 1, Putin said any negotiations must take both sides’ interests into account.

# ARMS & THE CHIP

### Every war leaves ruins and patents. From Greek fire to AI drones, the winners own the patents and the gold that pays for them.

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!mEqn!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0f7d568a-052b-4887-96eb-444a8cd9caac_1670x942.jpeg)

Before we march, let us define our terms, because the phrase “**technological development**“ is used by politicians, central bankers and venture capitalists with the same precision a drunk uses a lamppost: more for support than illumination.

A technological development is **the process by which new knowledge is turned into new capability, a better way of doing something**, or a way of doing something that was previously impossible. Economists, following the Austrian Joseph Schumpeter, break it into three distinct stages, and the distinction matters for investors because each stage rewards a different kind of capital.
